Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my Slater-Marietta home lose power more than friends in Greenville?

Longer feeder lines through heavier tree cover, mostly. Foothills addresses sit farther down distribution runs with more exposure between them and the substation, so storms find more opportunities. That exposure is also why standby generators concentrate up here: the outage math is simply different.

Can a mini-split really heat an old mill house through winter?

Modern cold-climate units can, and they are often the best retrofit answer for homes without ducts. Capacity holds well below freezing on current equipment, and multi-zone setups cover separated rooms old floor plans create. The load calculation confirms sizing against the specific house.

My crawl space always smells damp. Is that a plumbing leak or something else?

It can be either, so the inspection checks both. A supply or drain leak keeps the space wet from inside, while ground moisture and poor drainage wet it from below, and foothills lots see plenty of the latter. Finding the source first keeps the fix from being an expensive guess.

Is it safe to keep using a fuse box or very old panel?

Age alone is not the verdict, but capacity and condition usually are. Panels from that era were designed around a fraction of modern demand, and overheating, corrosion, or obsolete breakers change the risk picture. An evaluation documents the actual condition and states plainly whether replacement is a safety matter or a someday project.

Which nearby communities are on the same routes?

Marietta, Travelers Rest, and Taylors share the northern county dispatch. The chat team can confirm any foothills address.
